commit: 91eef58 (v0.16.0 + RFC-8 bug-half fix), recalibrated with warmup exclusion after round-1 review
box: 16-core reference box (audit 2026-07-28), single-thread BLAS, median of 5 steady reps (1 warmup excluded)
notes: Thresholds are deliberately generous: CI runners are slower and noisier than the reference box, and the gate exists to catch structural regressions (a lost support-compression or cached-W win), not 20% noise. Ratio checks are machine-speed invariant to first order and carry the tighter limits; absolute checks are large multiples of reference-box medians. The tensor benchmark excludes one warmup fit per case (import/cache effects measured at 1.5-3x steady state were the dominant rep-to-rep spread in CI).
ci_observed: perf-gate runs on ubuntu-latest (2026-07-29, n=30k, warmup-excluded): steady medians 1.21-1.36x this box (0.328/0.216/1.192/0.590 vs 0.249/0.165/0.888/0.435); steady ratios tensor_multiplier_exact 3.63 and tensor_multiplier_discrete 2.73 (headroom 1.65x/1.83x to the 6.0/5.0 limits); steady rep spreads 1-5%; flagship median 1.02-1.04s; flagship deviance/effective_df rel_dev measured 0.000 vs reference-box values

tensor_multiplier_exact.note: reference 3.57, CI-observed 3.63-3.67 warmup-excluded (1.63-1.65x headroom); the pre-arc reversion is 7.2x and MUST trip, so this limit cannot be widened past ~7

tensor_multiplier_discrete.note: reference 2.64, CI-observed 2.73-2.76 warmup-excluded (1.81-1.83x headroom); the 3.8x pre-arc discrete multiplier sits inside runner noise of any non-flapping limit, so this check only guards catastrophic tensor-path blowups

absolute_multiple.note: per-case median vs reference-box median. 5.0 makes the 6.6x pre-arc base-exact reversion trip on ANY machine (0.249*6.6=1.64s > 1.25s limit), unlike the previous 8.0 which relied on the runner being >=1.21x slower than the reference box; observed CI medians still leave ~3.8x headroom

limit 1.69s: the 2.48x pre-arc flagship reversion is 2.10s on the reference box itself, so 2.0 catches it machine-independently; CI-observed median 1.02-1.04s leaves 1.66x headroom on a benchmark whose steady spread is ~2%; this is the gate's tightest check and is anchored to a different machine -- if it ever flaps, do NOT widen the multiple (that re-disarms the reversion catch): switch to a self-calibrating anchor (measure a cheap fixed workload in the same run and express the limit as a ratio to it)

expected.note: recorded fit outputs on the reference box; identical data and a deterministic algorithm make these platform-stable, and a gate pass on timing alone must not certify a fit that silently computed something else
